brief.summary: A shared library of scanned service manuals, wiring diagrams and past repair notes, kept by volunteers at a neighborhood repair café run on donations.
brief.user: Gerald Pryce, a retired electrician who volunteers as a fixer at a monthly repair café in a church hall. He's handy with appliances but rarely uses the library and isn't patient with computers.
brief.moment: It's Saturday, mid-session. A visitor has brought in a 1990s Sunbeam stand mixer that hums but won't spin, and there's a line of people waiting behind her. Gerald needs to narrow the library's 1,400 documents down to the manual or wiring diagram for this mixer family. He also wants to see whether another volunteer has fixed the same fault before, and then focus on the one document with the motor brush and speed-control details. A pencil-written model number on the base reads either 2346 or 2348.
brief.data: There are 1,412 documents. Each has a type (service manual, user manual, wiring diagram, parts list, repair note), brand, model numbers, product category, year range, language, scan quality (good/faded/partial), page count and contributor. Kitchen appliances account for 318 documents and Sunbeam for 27. One Mixmaster 2346/2348 service manual from 1994 (22 pages, faded) was contributed by volunteer Ruth Okonjo. There are 340 past repair logs, each with a date, item, fault, outcome (fixed/partly fixed/not fixed) and fixer. Two logs from 2024 describe Mixmaster units that hummed without spinning; one was traced to worn carbon brushes. The café meets the second Saturday of each month and has 14 active volunteers.
